# Goban Studio v14.0.0

v14 keeps the four spaces and makes the app refined: easy to start,
polished on every screen, and tidy underneath. The app opens on Today,
Practice shows positions instead of a wall of names, your progress is
drawn where you can see it, and almost everything you do can be undone.
v14 reads everything v9–v13 saved; nothing has to be converted.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation. Your games, progress and settings are
kept outside the app — in `~/Library/Application Support/dev.hxddh.gobanstudio`
on macOS and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.hxddh.gobanstudio\Data` on Windows — so
replacing the app keeps them.

## Easier to start

- **The first launch lands on Today**, for everyone. One button starts
  lesson one, a gentle 9×9 game or a 19×19 game, depending on what you
  said you know. Beginners get a 13×13 step between 9×9 and 19×19.
- **Rules follow your language** if you are new: Chinese rules in Chinese,
  Korean rules in Korean, Japanese rules otherwise. If you already use the
  app, your rules stay as they are.
- **The placement quiz stops early** when the first four problems are all
  missed, instead of asking six more.
- **New game** names the board sizes plainly (13×13 is no longer labelled
  with the word for "middle game" in Chinese) and shows the time control.
- **Only one copy runs.** Opening the app again, or double-clicking an
  `.sgf` while it is open, brings up the window that is already there.
- **Updates and the optional networks work through an HTTP proxy** (the
  one in your system settings, or `HTTPS_PROXY`), and a download that is
  interrupted continues where it stopped. The sidebar shows when an update
  is downloading or ready.
- **Settings → Data → Show data folder** opens the folder your games are
  in. The package READMEs now say correctly where that is, how to open
  an unsigned app on macOS 15, and what uninstalling leaves behind. The
  `.dmg` has an Applications shortcut to drag the app onto.

## Practice

- **Positions, not names.** A topic is a grid of small boards, each marked
  as tried, solved, due for review or mastered.
- **A problem's name no longer gives the answer away.** Until you solve it
  you see only the goal ("Black to live"); the name of the shape or
  technique appears afterwards.
- **Today's path** merges rows of the same kind ("Ladder · 4 problems"),
  says why each row is there, and shows how many reviews are waiting. You
  choose the day's size: 3, 5 or 10.
- **Reviews come before new problems**, at most 12 a day, so the pile
  stops growing while new problems keep arriving.
- **Difficulty is Level 1–5**, each with the ranks it is meant for (≈),
  instead of "Beginner … Challenge".
- **Your solving level is honest.** Only the first time you meet a problem
  counts, so reviewing cannot push the level up. The stretch problem is
  one level above yours, not two.
- A miss says when the problem will come back, and nothing moves on by
  itself.

## Today

- **Your progress**: your level with its history as a small line, the
  problems you have mastered (by topic if you ask), the last four weeks as
  dots, and recent milestones. There are no streaks.

## Playing and reviewing

- **Undo almost everywhere.** Deleting a game shows "Deleted · Undo"
  instead of asking first. In a game, a move you took back can be redone.
  In a review, comments, marks and variations have undo and redo.
- **A stone tried in a review is a trial line**: keep it or discard it. It
  is no longer saved by accident, and comments are saved when you leave the
  box and when you quit.
- **←/→ during a game** no longer drop you into the review.
- **Passing** is asked in place, without a sheet, for your first pass and
  for the pass that ends the game.
- **Count again.** If you marked the wrong group dead, you can recount a
  game after confirming; the result and the rating step are replaced.
- **A game with undo or hints is not rated**, and the result says so.
- **Narrow windows** keep the clock, Pass and Undo in view under the board.

## Library

- **Unfinished games have their own group**: continue one, just look at
  it, or clear them.
- From six games on you can sort, filter and search; rows show relative
  dates and the game's biggest swing.
- **Import** by pasting an SGF, or several files at once (with Undo). A
  file that holds many games lets you choose one or import them all, and
  every warning about a file is shown.
- **Openings and joseki** is a section of its own, with less noise.
  **Open board** gives you a free board for placing stones.

## Board, sound and Settings

- **A darker board in dark mode**, and an optional high-contrast board
  (chosen for you when the system forces colours). The last move is marked
  with a thin ring. Thumbnails are drawn for each board size and are
  readable on 19×19.
- **Sound volume**: Off, Quiet, Normal, Loud.
- **Settings** has seven panes — General, Board, Playing, You, Engines,
  Data, About — and none of them scrolls. There is one "Your level" row.
- Text in lessons, notes and About can be selected and copied. The
  shortcuts sheet lists every shortcut. Review toolbar buttons have their
  own icons and visible tooltips.
- **Messages.** Notices come in four kinds, can be closed, and errors look
  like errors and stay. A screen that breaks shows a card with Try again
  instead of freezing; lessons, classics and game files that are still
  loading say so and offer Retry. The wording was gone over in all four
  languages: messages about your data say what happened, whether your data
  is safe, and what to do.

## Fixed

- **Library → Rename** did nothing. It works again.
- **Counting.** When every stone of one side is dead, the open board now
  belongs to the other side. Before, it counted as neutral, and the side
  that owned the whole board could lose by komi. All three rule sets.
- **The Chinese opening** was taught on the wrong points. The lesson now
  uses Q16, Q3 and R9 (high: Q9).
- **The computer** passes on a settled board and no longer fills its own
  eyes when the offline engine is playing.
- **The stronger network** is no longer switched off for the session when
  you undo while it is thinking.
- **SGF.** Older files with long property names read correctly; files
  that do not name their encoding are guessed (GBK, Big5, Shift_JIS, EUC),
  with a warning; a komi written in hundredths (`KM[375]`, `KM[650]`)
  reads as 7.5 or 6.5 points, not 375; dates are kept as written; an
  export made while you look at a variation still carries the result.
- **Lessons.** Over-long steps were split or shortened (377 steps now),
  and a board in the ko-counting lesson that did not follow from the
  step before it was corrected.
- **Classics.** Four more commented moments: Jowa's three moves in the
  Blood-vomiting game, and AlphaGo's answer to move 78 in its fourth game
  with Lee Sedol.

## Under the hood

- The code is checked by a linter on every change; it is what found the
  Rename bug. Every sheet and every menu item is opened by a test.
- An update's signature now names its version, so an old release cannot
  be offered as a new one. Signing runs in a protected environment and
  never in a rehearsal.
- The code was put in order: the interface's strings are filed by area,
  the largest modules were split, the stylesheet was rebuilt on its
  tokens, and the app starts with one language loaded instead of four.
- The tool the desktop shell is built with is pinned by hash, and changes
  to the shell are compiled and tested on macOS and Windows before they
  are merged.

## Known limits

- **Not checked by people.** There has been no usability test, no strong
  player's review (the corrected Chinese opening, the new classic notes
  and all lessons added in v13 included), no native-speaker review of the
  Chinese, Korean and Japanese text (the new Korean and Japanese strings
  are the developer's own), and no session with a real screen reader.
- **The builds are not code-signed.** macOS and Windows warn on first
  launch; the table above and the README in each download say what to do.
  Signing needs certificates only the project's owner can obtain. This
  release also carries no update signature: no key is configured yet.
- **There is no Windows installer.** The download is still a zip: no
  Start menu entry, no uninstaller, and opening `.sgf` files by
  double-click needs one command from the README.
- **Platform code has not been tried by hand.** Running a single copy,
  reading the system proxy and Show data folder (new in v14), and waiting
  for the last save on quit (from v13), compile and pass their tests on
  macOS and Windows, but nobody has used them on a real Mac or PC.
- **The opening book does not have the Chinese opening.** The wrong label
  was removed; the real line is missing until the book is rebuilt with
  KataGo. The KataGo check of the lessons has not been run again for the
  steps that changed.
- **No Traditional Chinese interface.** A name written only in Chinese
  characters is drawn in the interface language's font, whoever it
  belongs to; names with kana or hangul get their own.
- **Count again** is not offered for rated games finished before v14.
- **Content.** 15 of the 20 classics have only their headline note; the
  problem bank tops out at about 5 kyu; the first time you see a problem
  it is always Black to play.
- The guess at the encoding of a file that does not name one can be
  wrong for short names; it warns when it guesses.
